$comment: Canonical Cairndex keyboard/menu table (plan 3 §7). This file is the SINGLE
source of truth for the native menu bar and its accelerators. It is consumed
twice: TypeScript imports it for the in-app shortcut reference and menu-action
typing, and the Tauri shell include_str!s it at compile time and BUILDS the
native menu from it (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/keymap.rs). Because the menu is
built from this table rather than mirroring it, the two cannot drift.
'accelerator' is a muda accelerator string handled by the OS before the webview
sees the event; it is therefore always modifier-based, so it can never swallow a
keystroke meant for a text field. 'keys' lists the bare-key bindings the web app
Shift+Enter (Open in Default App) is the one accelerator whose modifier is Shift
alone, at the owner's request (2026-08-24). Checked before agreeing: nothing in
the app reads Shift+Enter, and the note box's line break comes from plain Enter —
it has no keydown handler at all — so this takes no keystroke away. The residual
cost is that Shift held over while typing a note turns the next Enter into a file
launch instead of a newline; plain Enter is unaffected.
handles itself in the focused viewer (app/viewer/player/useShortcuts.ts); those
work identically in the browser and in the shell.
'browserReserved' marks accelerators a browser intercepts before the page (tab
switching, address bar, devtools, history). They are unusable on the web and
become available only inside the shell — that is the D5 shortcut audit.
RULE (owner, 2026-07-19): give an item an accelerator ONLY when no 'keys' entry
already covers it. An accelerator is reserved application-wide, so duplicating a
bare viewer key burns a global combo for a command reachable only with the viewer
open. Playback therefore carries accelerators solely on Previous/Next File, which
have no bare-key binding at all once a video loads (the arrows become seek).
'requires' gates enablement: 'host-file' waits for a selection this Mac can hand
to the OS, 'new-folder' waits for a File Browser directory a folder can be
created in (write mode on, browse scope), 'server' items wait for desktop
bootstrap to reach a
verified server, 'library' items for an unlocked mounted workspace, 'viewer' for
an open media viewer, and 'viewer-video' for a viewer showing a video (an image
bundle has no player, so those commands would be enabled but dead). null means
always enabled.
'Reveal in Finder' and 'Open in Default App' are macOS wording, because the shell
is macOS-only
(ADR-0012). The per-platform strings the context menus use live in
platform/index.ts as hostLabels.revealFile ('Show in File Explorer', 'Show in
File Manager'); a second desktop platform would have to set this item's text at
runtime from those rather than read it from here.
'predefined' selects a Tauri built-in menu item (OS-localized, native behavior);
such entries carry no id of their own, and their accelerator is the OS's — where
one is written here it is recorded for the in-app shortcut reference and to
reserve the combo, never registered by us. Full Screen is predefined for exactly
that reason: AppKit inserts its own Enter Full Screen item into the View menu
unless the app already has one bound to toggleFullScreen:, so a custom item of
ours produced two entries doing the same thing (owner, 2026-09-01). A 'label' on
a predefined entry sets its initial text; macOS still swaps Enter/Exit itself. The App menu's hide/hide-others/
show-all trio is where macOS's Cmd-H and Cmd-Opt-H come from: a fully custom menu
bar with no Hide item leaves those combos dead, which is what happened (owner,
2026-08-23). Their accelerators are the OS's, not this table's, so the keymap test's
IMPLICIT list is what keeps a future explicit item from shadowing them.
